analysis.title: FirstEnergy Corp. (FE): First Take: EPS beat vs. GSe and Street; incremental transmission capex opportunities in focus
key_insights: FE reported 3Q26 core EPS of $0.98 vs GS estimate $0.92 and FactSet consensus $0.90, a $0.06 beat vs GS.
FE reaffirmed 2026 core EPS guidance of $2.62-$2.82 (GS estimate $2.74) and guided to the midpoint or slightly better.
FE affirmed its 6%-8% long-term EPS CAGR and expects to be near the top end.
FE expects to raise transmission investment by 25% in its next capital plan, taking the current $19bn of capex through 2030 to about $24bn through 2031.
The added transmission spend reflects replacement of aging equipment, grid efficiency, reliability projects and large load demand.

FE contracted an incremental ~1.5 GW of data center demand in the quarter, bringing total contracted large load to ~7.9 GW and the demand pipeline to 27 GW, with the biggest increase in West Virginia.
Quarterly variance vs GS was driven by higher EPS at Distribution (+$0.03) and Corporate (+$0.08), partly offset by lower EPS at Integrated (-$0.01) and Transmission (-$0.03).
On the income statement, slightly higher gross margin, lower amortization expense and lower income taxes drove the beat, partly offset by higher operating expenses than GS expected.
GS expects the call to focus on incremental transmission capex and its effect on earnings growth, regulatory activity in NJ, MD and WV, and data center contracting progress.

GS key call questions: pace of pipeline conversion from 7.9 GW contracted, share of added transmission capex tied to large load, NJ and MD rate case debate points, and next generation project in West Virginia beyond Maidsville including the GenCo structure.

market_movers.rationale: 3Q26 core EPS beat, reaffirmed guidance, and higher transmission capex and data center contracting support the longer-term growth outlook. GS sees a 14.5% upside to the $53 target from $46.27.

Pension expense and/or interest expense coming in higher than expected.
